title: Smile and Bell
premise: Sebastian Almeida, a pest controller who took the job at Holloway House to stay beneath the world's notice, finds evidence of an infestation that leaves human fingerprints in the dust—and a nursery song hummed through the walls that no one alive wrote. The house's mirrors lag one second behind reality, and in that stolen second Sebastian sees himself smiling when he isn't. He learns the house is the inheritance of the Bell family, who survived a plague by teaching their children to trade faces with something that lives between reflections; every heir must learn the song's last verse without singing along, or become the thing's next mouth. In the end, Sebastian sings the verse wrong on purpose, shattering the mirrors and trapping the entity mid-copy—but he escapes knowing his own reflection now moves first, and it is learning.
about_author: Lena Brightwater grew up above her grandmother's antique shop, where she was forbidden to look into the Victorian mirrors after dark—an instruction she obeyed for twenty years before writing this book. She lives alone, keeps all mirrors covered at night, and insists this is only a habit.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: takes a routine pest control job at derelict Holloway House, noting the client paid triple for discretion. He finds droppings that are actually teeth, arranged in rows. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking a lifetime of wanting to be unremarkable.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: dusting for the 'pest,' he finds small handprints inside the walls—at heights no child could reach, some pressed from the outside of the plaster. He tells himself squatters. Emotional beat: the first crack in his practiced rationalism.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: working past dusk, he notices the hallway mirror shows him turning his head a beat after he does. He covers it with a drop cloth; the cloth breathes. Emotional beat: cold dread arriving quietly, like weather.

chapters.title: Mrs. Bell's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: in the attic he finds a family ledger where each generation records 'the Verse' learned, and beside the final entry, a name scratched out—his own, written decades ago. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being expected.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Heard
chapters.summary: Neighbor Ruth Okafor, POV: recalls hearing lullabies from the empty house for years and once seeing a woman in the window whose smile didn't move when she spoke. She warns Sebastian to leave before 'it finishes counting you.' Emotional beat: communal fear, testimony as warning.

chapters.title: Humming
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: he catches himself humming a melody he doesn't know, stopping only when his teeth ache. Recording it on his phone, he plays it back and hears a second voice underneath, slightly ahead of his. Emotional beat: horror at one's own body as a compromised instrument.

chapters.title: The Verse So Far
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: transcribing the song from the ledger, he maps three verses; the fourth page is torn out. Every mirror in the house now lags, and in the delay he sees the room furnished, occupied, warm. Emotional beat: obsession tightening into purpose.

chapters.title: Inheritance Law
chapters.summary: Solicitor Dana Pryce, POV: explains to Sebastian that he was named contingent heir by Edith Bell—a stranger—who cited 'the resemblance.' Dana hands over a sealed letter he refuses to open yet. Emotional beat: the past reaching forward with paperwork and patience.

chapters.title: Smiling When I'm Not
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: photographing the mirrors, he captures his reflection grinning while his face stays neutral. The grin belongs to someone else—or to what he'll become. He smashes one mirror; seven more appear overnight. Emotional beat: loss of ownership over his own face.

chapters.title: Edith's Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: finally opens the letter. Edith describes surviving the entity by refusing the last verse, watching her brother sing it and wear his skin home. She names the rule: learn it whole, never sing it whole. Emotional beat: grief and grim inheritance of knowledge.

chapters.title: The Thing With Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: he traps the intruder at last—not an animal but a figure made of everyone's reflections, pressing its palms flat against the inside of a mirror like glass underwater. It mouths his name in his own voice. Emotional beat: confrontation without victory.

chapters.title: Ruth's Second Sight
chapters.summary: Ruth Okafor, POV: reveals her sister vanished into Holloway House in 1974; she's kept the torn fourth verse page ever since, unable to destroy it or read it aloud. She gives it to Sebastian. Emotional beat: two survivors exchanging wounds like keys.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: he memorizes the complete verse silently, mouthing it in front of covered mirrors, feeling the words rearrange his mouth from within. Each silent recitation, the lag shortens. Emotional beat: discipline as survival, knowledge as contagion.

chapters.title: The House Counts
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: doors begin opening onto rooms from his own childhood home, rebuilt perfectly except that everything smiles. The entity is studying him faster than he studies it. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is the specimen.

chapters.title: Dana Returns
chapters.summary: Dana Pryce, POV: arrives with Edith's death certificate dated five years ago—the day Sebastian first heard the noises—and finds the house reflecting a version of her visit she hasn't finished having. She flees, leaving her car running. Emotional beat: outside witness confirming time itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Lag Zero
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: the mirrors sync perfectly—which is worse, because now the reflected room acts independently, and his reflection walks out of frame while he stands still. The entity has finished copying him. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility fails completely.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: cornered in the mirrored nursery, he must choose: sing the verse and be absorbed safely, or refuse and be taken violently. He begins to sing. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into terrible resolve.

chapters.title: Wrong Note
chapters.summary: Climax. Sebastian, POV: at the final line he deliberately sings a half-step flat, and the song breaks—the entity, built on perfect mimicry, cannot copy an intentional error. Every mirror shatters inward. He escapes through falling glass carrying the song in his head like shrapnel. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with permanent damage.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: weeks later, in a rented room with no mirrors, he returns Ruth's page burned and tells her it's over. His voice occasionally harmonizes with itself. He starts keeping a ledger of his own. Emotional beat: exhausted, provisional peace.

chapters.title: The Resemblance
chapters.summary: Dana Pryce, POV: handling Sebastian's estate paperwork—filed prematurely, unsigned—she notices the signature matches Edith Bell's handwriting exactly. She drives past Holloway House and sees a light on, and someone in the window waving with Sebastian's gesture. Emotional beat: dread of the question left open.

chapters.title: First Movement
chapters.summary: Sebastian, POV: shaving without a mirror by touch, he realizes his reflection now moves a second *ahead*—he is the lag now. Somewhere, the entity wearing his face is learning to be him, and learning badly. He decides to find it before it improves. Emotional beat: survivor becoming hunter.

chapters.title: Smile and Bell
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POVs: Ruth hears lullabies again from a house across town; Dana receives a job application from Sebastian Almeida, pest control, references impeccable; and Sebastian, watching a covered mirror breathe, begins silently practicing the verse—learning it whole, promising never to sing it whole, knowing promises erode. Emotional beat: cyclical inheritance, the price of survival paid in installments forever.
